title: Reliability Initiative Lifecycle: Commitment Phases & Automated Handoff Protocol
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: Define and ship an initiative lifecycle and automated handoff protocol that closes gaps between SLO ownership, oncall rotations, and product/infra rollouts. This ticket is the PM-led charter to (1) codify commitment phases (Draft -> Committed -> Live -> Sunset), (2) design a machine-readable initiative ledger for per-initiative error-budget allowances and replenishment rules, and (3) prototype an automated handoff flow that creates and reconciles follow-up tasks across teams when error budgets cross thresholds. The outcome should reduce missed SLAs after handoffs, speed up remediation, and make error-budget allocation transparent for roadmapping and OKR alignment.
tasks: Interview oncall leads and SREs to surface current pain points with handoffs and ownership
Draft initiative lifecycle state machine and mapping to SLO phases (Draft, Committed, Monitoring, Escalation, Rollback, Sunset)
Define machine-readable fields for initiative ledger: owner, SLI targets, error-budget allocation, replenish cadence, rollback triggers
Prototype a reconciliation runner that reads ledger and opens follow-up Linear tickets (or updates existing ones) when thresholds are crossed
Design UI affordances for Console: Initiative card with error-budget runway, next-action, and delegated owner
Coordinate with infra to surface metrics from SLI data pipeline and wire to the ledger
acceptance_criteria: A documented lifecycle spec in Confluence with state transitions and required signoffs
A JSON schema for initiative ledger fields checked into the repo
A simple prototype that auto-creates follow-up tickets in Linear when an initiative's error budget drops below 25%
A Console mock that shows initiative status and next recommended action (can be static images for MVP)
Stakeholder review complete with SRE, Platform, and two product teams signed off
comments: 2025-01-10 Aisha Patel: Kickoff — gathered initial list of stakeholders (SRE: Priya Rao, Platform: Diego Martinez, Product: Elena Ford). Plan to do 6 interviews across SRE and product this week.

2025-01-16 Marcus Chen: Interview round complete. Common themes: handoffs often lack explicit timeboxed remediation tasks; oncall rotations lose context; no single source-of-truth for allocated error-budget across subteams.

2025-01-20 Marcus Chen: Draft lifecycle state machine uploaded to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.example.com/display/Reliability/Initiative+Lifecycle. Requested PM and SRE feedback — Priya requested explicit 'Rollback Approval' gate for high-risk rollouts.

2025-01-24 Diego Martinez (Platform): Raised a concern that automated ticket creation should not overwhelm small teams; suggested bucketing low-impact alerts into a consolidated 'initiative-runway' ticket rather than multiple child tasks.
2025-01-28 Aisha Patel: Decision — MVP will create a single follow-up ticket per initiative (with subtasks) to avoid noise; we will iterate on finer-grained automations after measuring signal/noise.

2025-01-30 Marcus Chen: Prototype ledger schema (initial) pushed to GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/initiative-ledger/pull/12. Contains fields: owner, slo_target, error_budget_total, error_budget_remaining, replenish_policy, rollback_thresholds, monitoring_contacts.

2025-02-01 Priya Rao (SRE): Reviewed schema, suggested adding 'oncall_rotation_window' and 'escalation_playbook_link' fields. Also requested that the runner annotate tickets with relevant SLI slices and time ranges for reproducibility.
2025-02-02 Aisha Patel: Updated acceptance criteria to require stakeholder signoffs. Next steps: wire SLI feed to ledger staging and schedule design review with Console UX on 2025-02-10.
